newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli industrial output grew 5.5 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Israeli industrial output grew 5.5 pct in 1996.

text.p: Israel's industrial production grew a seasonally adjusted 2.6 percent in December, following two months of declines, bringing the full-year gain to 5.5 percent, the Central Bureau of Statistics said on Tuesday.
On an unadjusted basis, industrial production was 11.7 percent higher for the month.

Growth in industrial output slowed from 1995's level of 8.5 percent and showed a steady slowing throughout 1996. Output grew at a seasonally adjusted 0.4 percent monthly rate in the first quarter, slowing to 0.2 percent in the second and third and 0.3 percent in the fourth.

The bureau said that for full-year 1996, the sharpest growth in production came in electronic and communications equipment, which showed an 18 percent rise, followed by electronic components, which rose 15 percent.
Other big gains were recorded in chemicals and chemical products (11 percent) and non-ferrous minerals (17 percent).
Food, beverage and tobacco output was unchanged for the year, while textile and apparels was down four percent.
Industrial employment grew by only 1.5 percent, the bureau said.
